docs.title: bank-stmt-dlh
docs.text:
Bank statement PDFs (HDFC Bank current account layout) go in. A reconciled ledger comes out, with category, recurring-payment, cash and runway reports. It runs on a laptop with DuckDB, or as a scheduled Databricks job that reads the PDFs from an S3-compatible bucket and serves an AI/BI dashboard and a weekly cash report by email.

Deterministic first. Parsing, reconciliation, rules, recurring detection, reports and the dashboard are plain code and SQL. The one optional AI step is Jev (TypeSafe AI), used only for payments the rules cannot place, behind a confidence gate.

PDF statements  (local folder | S3-compatible bucket | SharePoint folder)
   -> bronze   file list + raw parsed lines
   -> silver   reconciled statements + transactions (weekly/monthly duplicates tagged once)
   -> gold     categorized facts, recurring series, views  -> reports, dashboard, weekly email
Step Method Parse and reconcile pdfplumber + balance arithmetic (src/extract.py) Channel, counterparty, txn_id regex and hashing (src/normalize.py) Categorize payee map, then rules, then founder logic (config/*.yaml, src/categorize.py) Recurring and yearly payments gap and amount test, plus a declared list (src/recurring.py) Reports, dashboard, weekly email SQL views and plain rendering Leftovers Jev, optional, confidence 0.9 or more

Never load an unreconciled statement

Every statement is checked against the bank's own STATEMENT SUMMARY: debit and credit counts, totals and the closing balance. One that does not match goes to quarantine and is never loaded further.

docs.title: Where to go
docs.text:
• Getting started: run the synthetic samples in two minutes, then your own statements.
  • Configuration: .env, config/settings.yaml, payees, rules, categories.
  • Databricks lakehouse: bucket, secrets, deploy, jobs, dashboard.
  • Data model: bronze, silver and gold tables and views.
  • Cookbooks: the optional Microsoft 365 pieces, a SharePoint statement source and the weekly report mail.
  • Process: how changes are made (OpenSpec, AI-DLC), and how the public copy is produced.

Source: github.com/senthilsweb/bank-stmt-dlh. MIT licence.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Two files, one rule: secrets in .env, names in config/settings.yaml. Nothing personal is in code.

docs.title: .env
docs.text:
Variable Used for PDF_PASSWORD Opens the statement PDFs. Empty for the synthetic samples STATEMENTS_DIR Folder with the PDFs (local runs, make upload). Relative paths are from the repo root TYPESAFE_API_KEY Jev, optional. Empty means no AI step at all DATABRICKS_HOST, DATABRICKS_TOKEN, DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH Workspace, token and SQL warehouse path DATABRICKS_USER Your workspace login. Code is deployed under /Users/<DATABRICKS_USER>/bank-stmt-dlh DATABRICKS_CATALOG Catalog for the local SQL runner (same as catalog in settings) ALERT_EMAIL Who gets a mail when a job fails (defaults to DATABRICKS_USER) MINIO_ENDPOINT, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY, MINIO_SECRET_KEY, MINIO_BUCKET S3-compatible statement source SP_* SharePoint app and folder ids (cookbook) MAIL_* Weekly report sender, recipients and mode (cookbook)

.env.sample is the contract and is kept complete.

docs.title: config/settings.yaml
docs.text:
company_name: ConceptLabs        # report and dashboard title
catalog: bank_stmt_dlh           # Unity Catalog catalog, created once by hand
secret_scope: bank-stmt-dlh      # Databricks secret scope filled by `make secrets`
minio_bucket: bank-stmt-dlh      # statement_source: minio
minio_prefix: statements/        # monthly under the prefix, weekly under <prefix>weekly/
jev_confidence_threshold: 0.9    # Jev label accepted at or above this
review_amount_threshold: 5000    # unlabelled rows at or above this (INR) need a person
statement_source: minio          # minio | sharepoint
report_body_currency: INR        # weekly email body: INR | USD (PDFs are always sent in both)

src/settings.py reads this file next to the package, so the same code runs on a laptop and in the deployed workspace copy.

docs.title: Categories, payees, rules
docs.text:
Categorization is deterministic and ordered. First match wins.

  1. Payee map, config/merchant_map.yaml. A name matches as whole words in the cleaned counterparty, case insensitive. An entry can be a plain name, re:<regex> for narrations the bank splits oddly, or a mapping with direction and from / until dates.
  2. Rules, config/rules.yaml. A regex over counterparty and narration, optionally limited to a direction.
  3. Founder logic, the founder block of the payee map. Every debit to the founder is operations; a credit that matches an earlier debit of the same amount is a loan repayment, any other credit is founder funding.
  4. Stored Jev label, then Jev for what is left, only with a key and only at confidence 0.9 or more.
  5. Otherwise unclassified, or human-intervention-required when the amount is at or above the review threshold or the row is a credit.

config/categories.yaml is the master list with a type per category (income, expense, statutory, debt, transfer, funding, operations). config/recurring_declared.yaml lists payments that repeat but cannot be detected (yearly, fewer than three occurrences) and engagements that have ended.

Every row carries category_source (map, rule, founder, jev, unclassified, review) and a confidence, so a label can always be traced.

docs.title: Jev, the only AI step
docs.text: Jev is a decision model, not a text-generating LLM. It answers a typed choice question with a probability and a confidence. It sees only Counterparty: X. Channel: upi. Direction: debit., never amounts, dates or account numbers. Every answer is stored, so the same request is never sent twice. No key means no call.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: Three schemas in one catalog (catalog in config/settings.yaml). Locally the same shape lands in data/silver/*.parquet and data/bank.duckdb.

docs.title: Bronze: what arrived
docs.text:
Table One row per Columns of note bronze.statement_files file seen in the source object_key, etag, file_sha256, size_bytes, source, statement_kind, reconciled, parser_version bronze.raw_lines parsed transaction line, before any cleaning file_sha256, seq, txn_date, narration, ref_no, value_date, amount, balance, direction

A file is new when its content hash is new. A moved or renamed copy of a loaded file is only re-registered.

docs.title: Silver: reconciled
docs.text:
Table One row per Columns of note silver.statements reconciled statement period_from, period_to, opening, closing, debits, credits, txn_count, statement_kind silver.transactions transaction, once txn_id, txn_date, narration, ref_no, amount, balance, direction, signed_amount, channel, counterparty_clean, statement_kind silver.transaction_sources appearance of a line in a file txn_id, file_sha256, statement_kind, is_duplicate, duplicate_of_file silver.quarantine file that failed reconciliation file, errors, quarantined_at

txn_id is a hash of date, reference, amount and running balance. Narration is left out because weekly and monthly statements print it differently for some lines; the balance keeps look-alike lines apart. channel is upi, upi-autopay, card, imps, neft, rtgs, cheque, bank-interest or other.

docs.title: Gold: facts, reference, reports
docs.text:
Table Written by Purpose gold.fact_transactions 03 Every transaction with category, category_source, category_confidence, is_founder gold.recurring_series 03 Detected monthly and yearly series: payee, cadence, typical amount, last seen, next expected, status gold.review_queue 03 Rows that need a person gold.jev_labels 03 Every Jev answer, keyed by the request text, so it is never asked twice gold.dim_category, gold.payee_map, gold.category_rules, gold.recurring_declared, gold.settings 01 The YAML configuration as tables, so SQL users can see what each label is based on gold.fx_rates 04 One ECB USD/INR reference rate per date used gold.weekly_cash_snapshot, gold.weekly_cash_snapshot_lines 04 Append-only: each weekly report as sent gold.report_log 04 Every send: week, mode, version, recipients, status

Views in databricks/sql/20_gold_views.sql, all plain SQL: monthly_flow, monthly_flow_long, spend_by_category_month, category_totals, upcoming_payments, founder_monthly, funding_received, review_summary, statement_status, duplicate_lines, category_source_mix, kpis, cashflow_daily, balance_daily.

docs.title: Reconciliation rule
docs.text: For each statement, the parser recomputes from the rows: debit count, credit count, debit total, credit total and the last running balance, and compares them with the bank's STATEMENT SUMMARY. Direction of each row comes from the change in running balance. Any mismatch, including a balance break between two rows, quarantines the file.

docs.title: Databricks lakehouse
docs.text: The same parser runs inside a scheduled Databricks job. Raw PDFs stay in your bucket; each one is downloaded to temporary disk, parsed, reconciled and dropped. Nothing is kept in Databricks but the tables.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A Databricks workspace. Free Edition with serverless compute is enough.
  • An S3-compatible bucket: MinIO, AWS S3, Cloudflare R2. Use a key limited to that bucket, not a root account.
  • Optional: a Microsoft 365 tenant admin, once, if you want the SharePoint source or the weekly email.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
1. Fill the DATABRICKS_* and MINIO_* values in .env. In config/settings.yaml set statement_source: minio, minio_bucket and catalog.
  2. Create the catalog by hand in the SQL editor: CREATE CATALOG bank_stmt_dlh; (or your name).
  3. make db-init creates the bronze, silver and gold schemas.
  4. make secrets copies the PDF password, the Jev key and the bucket keys from .env into the secret scope. Groups: core, minio, sp, mail. An empty group that the configured source does not need is skipped.
  5. make deploy uploads src/, config/, databricks/sql/, assets/ and the notebooks to /Users/<DATABRICKS_USER>/bank-stmt-dlh. The repo is the source of truth; do not edit notebooks online.
  6. make etl creates or updates the two jobs and starts the ETL once.
  7. make dashboard generates the AI/BI dashboard definition from databricks/dashboards/build_dashboard.py and publishes it.

docs.title: Daily loop
docs.text:
make upload            # STATEMENTS_DIR -> bucket, then start the job (WEEKLY=1 for weekly statements)
make run               # start the ETL job now
make weekly-report     # run the weekly cash report now (WEEK_END=2026-10-18 FORCE=1 MODE=dry)
make deploy            # after a code or config change, then make run

Weekly statements go under statements/weekly/ in the bucket; everything else under the prefix is monthly.

docs.title: Jobs and notebooks
docs.text:
Job bank-stmt-dlh runs once a day at midnight IST. Task order: 02 (ingest) -> did it find new data? -> 01 (seed) -> 03 (gold). The last two run only when there is something new, or when the job is started with force=true (what make run does). Job bank-stmt-dlh-weekly-cash-report runs the same chain and then 04 every Monday 00:00 America/New_York.

Notebook What it does Deterministic? 01_reference_seed Copies categories, payee map, rules, declared payments and settings from config/*.yaml into gold tables Yes 02_ingest_bronze_silver Lists the bucket, skips content already loaded (SHA-256), parses, reconciles, tags weekly/monthly duplicates, merges to silver. Unreconciled files go to quarantine Yes 03_gold_build Categorizes, finds recurring payments, rebuilds gold tables and the views in databricks/sql/20_gold_views.sql Mostly. Holds the only AI call (Jev), if a key is set 04_weekly_cash_report Snapshots the week, fetches one USD/INR rate (ECB via Frankfurter), renders the email (INR or USD body, PDFs in both) and sends it through Microsoft Graph Yes jobs/b0_feasibility, jobs/b0_diagnose One-off checks that serverless compute can reach the bucket and parse a statement Yes jobs/s0_sharepoint_check, jobs/m0_mail_rate_check Health checks for the optional SharePoint source and mailer Yes

Notebooks find the deployed repo root from their own path and read catalog, secret scope and bucket from config/settings.yaml, so no user name or workspace id is in the code. SQL files use the token __CATALOG__, replaced at run time.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: Pages: Overview (cash, monthly outflow, runway), Spend, Recurring and yearly (next due, lapsed), Funding and founder, Cash flow by date (date-range filter), Data quality (statements loaded, quarantined files, duplicate lines, rows for review, reports sent). Every tile is SQL on the gold views; no model writes anything.

docs.title: Weekly cash report
docs.text:
One email per week with opening and closing balance, money in and out, spend by category, the largest movements, upcoming payments and the review queue. The body is in INR by default; two PDFs (INR and USD) are attached, at one stated exchange rate. Append-only snapshot tables keep every report as sent, so a resend reproduces what went out and past weeks do not change when rules are fixed later. gold.report_log records every send; a dry-run mode sends to one address only.

Sending needs a shared mailbox and a send-only Entra app limited to it: see the mail cookbook.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• A 403 from the bucket behind a proxy: rerun jobs/b0_diagnose, which probes list, HEAD and ranged GET.
  • A quarantined file is listed on the dashboard's Data quality tab with the reconciliation errors.
  • Secrets expire (SharePoint and mailer client secrets): renew, then make secrets.
  • Graph throttling (429) and 5xx answers are retried with backoff.

docs.title: Try it in two minutes
docs.text:
You need Python 3.12 or newer, uv and make.

Synthetic statements for a fictional company (ConceptLabs) are in samples/statements: four monthly statements (July to October 2026) and two weekly ones that overlap October, no password. The payee map shipped in config/ matches them.

git clone https://github.com/senthilsweb/bank-stmt-dlh.git
cd bank-stmt-dlh
make setup                                      # uv sync
make test                                       # 45 unit tests
STATEMENTS_DIR=samples/statements make extract  # parse and reconcile -> data/silver/*.parquet
make gold                                       # categorize, recurring -> data/bank.duckdb
make report                                     # print the reports

make extract prints one line per statement, reconciled or failed. make report shows the statements, the monthly summary, spend by category, the categorization source mix, upcoming payments (detected and declared, including one ended engagement) and the founder ledger.

6 statements, 80 transactions, 0 failed reconciliation

Regenerate the samples with python scripts/make_sample_statements.py. Make a text logo for your own company with python scripts/make_text_logo.py "Your Company" (used by the weekly report and its PDFs).

docs.title: Your own statements
docs.text:
1. cp .env.sample .env. Set PDF_PASSWORD (HDFC protects each statement with one) and STATEMENTS_DIR. Never commit .env.
  2. Edit config/merchant_map.yaml (known payees) and config/recurring_declared.yaml (yearly payments). The shipped files hold fictional names. config/rules.yaml and config/categories.yaml are generic and a good start.
  3. make extract, make gold, make report.

A statement for a running month is partial; drop the full one in after month end. Weekly statements may overlap monthly ones. Each line item is identified by date, reference, amount and running balance, so a line already loaded is counted once; the monthly text wins.

docs.title: What the parser expects
docs.text:
One text line per transaction, as pdfplumber extracts it from an HDFC current account statement:

DD/MM/YY  narration  <reference, 10 to 20 digits>  DD/MM/YY  amount  closing balance

Direction comes from the running balance, never from a column. The period comes from the From : ... To : ... line and the totals from the STATEMENT SUMMARY block. Another bank is one parser module that returns the same columns as src/extract.py.

docs.title: OpenSpec first, AI-DLC phases
docs.text:
Every non-trivial change starts as a folder openspec/changes/<name>/ with four files, before any code:

File Holds proposal.md Why, what changes, what is out of scope. Status and owner at the top specs/<area>/spec.md Requirements in SHALL form design.md How: tables, functions, decisions and their reasons tasks.md Owner prerequisites, execution bolts (B1, B2, ...), operations checks. Ticked as they land

Three phases. Intent is proposal, specs and design. Execution is the bolts; bolts that touch disjoint files run in parallel. Operations is validation on real statements (every statement reconciles, totals equal the bank's), then the specs and notes are updated. CLAUDE.md at the repo root states the rules for an AI pair.

The changes shipped so far: databricks-lakehouse, sharepoint-source, weekly-statements, weekly-cash-report, public-release. Each folder is readable on its own.

docs.title: Rules that do not bend
docs.text:
• Deterministic first. Parsing, reconciliation, rules and recurring detection are plain Python and SQL. AI only where rules cannot decide, behind a 0.9 confidence gate, and only ever sees the cleaned counterparty, channel and direction.
  • Never load an unreconciled statement.
  • Privacy. PDFs, Parquet and DuckDB are gitignored. .env is never committed. No real names, addresses, hosts or amounts in code, tests or docs. The synthetic statements in samples/ are the one tracked PDF set.
  • Python 3.12+, uv, make targets only. Docs short and plain.

docs.title: How this public copy is produced
docs.text: The code is developed in a private repository that holds one company's configuration. This public repository is an export of a branch: scripts/publish_public.py copies the tracked files, swaps in sample configuration and a generic logo, applies name replacements from a private mapping file, then scans every text file for real names, environment values, hosts and git authors. One hit stops the export. The first export is one squashed commit, so no private history is published. config/publish.yaml in this copy is an example of that mapping.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
• Add a bank: one parser module that returns the same columns as src/extract.py, plus a synthetic sample.
  • Add a category or rule: edit config/, run make test, then make deploy and make run.
  • Open a change folder under openspec/changes/ for anything larger and say what you intend before coding.

docs.title: Cookbook: send the weekly cash report through Microsoft Graph (one-time setup)
docs.text:
Goal: the Databricks job sends the weekly cash report from one shared mailbox, through Microsoft Graph sendMail, with an app that can send as that mailbox and no other. Needs a Microsoft 365 / Exchange admin. Design: openspec/changes/weekly-cash-report/design.md.

Why Graph and not SMTP: SMTP AUTH needs a mailbox password in a secret and Microsoft is phasing out basic authentication for it. Graph uses the app's own credentials, the same way the SharePoint reader does.

Item Value Sender noreply@<your domain> (MAIL_SENDER); replies go to finance-reports@<your domain> (MAIL_REPLY_TO). Both are shared mailboxes Entra app bank-stmt-dlh-mailer, single tenant, no redirect URI. Separate from the read-only SharePoint app Permission Microsoft Graph, Application, Mail.Send, admin consent Limit Exchange application access policy: this app may act only on the sender mailbox

docs.title: 1. The sender mailbox
docs.text: Use the existing shared mailbox, or create one: Exchange admin center (https://admin.exchange.microsoft.com) -> Recipients -> Mailboxes -> Add a shared mailbox -> name ConceptLabs Finance Reports, address finance-reports@.... A shared mailbox needs no licence. Note the full address: it is MAIL_SENDER.

docs.title: 2. Create the mailer app
docs.text:
1. https://entra.microsoft.com -> Entra ID -> App registrations -> New registration.
  2. Name bank-stmt-dlh-mailer; Single tenant; no redirect URI; Register.
  3. Copy Application (client) ID -> MAIL_CLIENT_ID. (The tenant id is the same as SP_TENANT_ID.)
  4. Certificates & secrets -> New client secret (12 or 24 months) -> copy the Value -> MAIL_CLIENT_SECRET. Set a calendar reminder 30 days before expiry.

docs.title: 3. Add the permission
docs.text:
API permissions -> Add a permission -> Microsoft Graph -> Application permissions -> Mail.Send -> Add -> Grant admin consent. Status shows a green tick.

Important: on its own, Mail.Send (application) lets the app send as any mailbox in the tenant. Do step 4 before using it.

docs.title: 4. Limit the app to the sender mailboxes (Exchange Online PowerShell, admin)
docs.text:
No Exchange admin page exists for this; it is PowerShell only. Azure Cloud Shell (https://shell.azure.com, choose PowerShell) works without installing anything, or brew install --cask powershell then pwsh on a Mac. 

Install-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement -Scope CurrentUser   # skip in Cloud Shell
Connect-ExchangeOnline

# a security group that holds only the mailboxes the app may send as
New-DistributionGroup -Name "bank-stmt-dlh-mailer-scope" -Type Security -Members finance-reports@<domain>,noreply@<domain>
Get-DistributionGroup bank-stmt-dlh-mailer-scope | Format-List PrimarySmtpAddress     # note the address
The group's address uses the default domain, e.g. bank-stmt-dlh-mailer-scope@<tenant>.onmicrosoft.com, not your own domain. Use that exact address below; @<your domain> fails with "identity of the policy scope could not be resolved". 
New-ApplicationAccessPolicy -AppId <MAIL_CLIENT_ID> -PolicyScopeGroupId bank-stmt-dlh-mailer-scope@<tenant>.onmicrosoft.com `
  -AccessRight RestrictAccess -Description "bank-stmt-dlh-mailer may act only on the finance-reports and noreply mailboxes"
Before the policy exists, Get-ApplicationAccessPolicy answers "couldn't be found": that means none is set, and Mail.Send lets the app send as any mailbox. Microsoft is moving to "RBAC for Applications" in Exchange Online for the same scoping; the policy above still works.

docs.title: 5. Check the limit (allow up to an hour for it to apply)
docs.text:
Test-ApplicationAccessPolicy -Identity finance-reports@<domain> -AppId <MAIL_CLIENT_ID>   # Granted
Test-ApplicationAccessPolicy -Identity noreply@<domain> -AppId <MAIL_CLIENT_ID>            # Granted
Test-ApplicationAccessPolicy -Identity <a personal mailbox> -AppId <MAIL_CLIENT_ID>        # Denied
From the repo: python scripts/graph_mail_check.py sends one plain test mail to MAIL_DRY_RUN_TO (HTTP 202); python scripts/graph_mail_check.py --as <a personal mailbox> must answer HTTP 403 once the policy is active.

docs.title: 6. Fill .env (gitignored; never paste secrets in chat or git)
docs.text:
MAIL_CLIENT_ID=<Application (client) ID>
MAIL_CLIENT_SECRET=<secret Value>
MAIL_SENDER=noreply@<domain>
MAIL_REPLY_TO=finance-reports@<domain>
MAIL_RECIPIENTS=first@example.com|First Person,second@example.com|Second Person
MAIL_DRY_RUN_TO=<your own address>
MAIL_MODE=dry
MAIL_RECIPIENTS: comma-separated address|Display Name; no commas inside a name. Keep MAIL_MODE=dry until the first dry run looks right.

docs.title: 7. Test (bolt M0)
docs.text: scripts/graph_mail_check.py sends one plain test mail to MAIL_DRY_RUN_TO from the sender mailbox, locally and from a serverless job. Expected: HTTP 202 and the mail arrives from the shared mailbox.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix AADSTS7000215 invalid client secret Copied the Secret ID, or it expired. Make a new secret 403 ErrorAccessDenied on sendMail Application access policy not applied yet (wait), or the mailbox is not in the scope group 403 Authorization_RequestDenied Mail.Send not consented, or Delegated chosen instead of Application 404 MailboxNotEnabledForRESTAPI / ResourceNotFound Wrong sender address, or the mailbox is not hosted in Exchange Online Mail lands in spam Send a dry run to yourself first and mark not spam; the shared mailbox uses your domain's SPF and DKIM Attachment rejected Over about 3 MB in this call; the report PDFs are far smaller

docs.title: Later additions
docs.text:
• Sender decision (2026-10-24): sending as finance-reports returned 403 from Graph for a while although Test-ApplicationAccessPolicy said Granted. noreply worked, so it is the sender and finance-reports is the Reply-To.
  • conceptlabs.com has SPF but no DKIM or DMARC. Turn on DKIM (Defender portal, Email authentication settings, DKIM; two CNAMEs at the DNS host) and add v=DMARC1; p=none to help Gmail trust the mail.
  • Run the real report to the dry-run address with python scripts/send_test_report.py <sunday>; the scheduled job is bank-stmt-dlh-weekly-cash-report (see the runbook page).

docs.title: Cookbook: SharePoint statement source (one-time setup)
docs.text:
Goal: let the Databricks job read the monthly statement PDFs from one SharePoint folder, read-only, with an Entra app, and nothing else in the tenant. Needs a Microsoft 365 / Entra admin. Design and reasons: openspec/changes/sharepoint-source/design.md.

Item Value (non-secret) SharePoint host <tenant>.sharepoint.com (root site, no /sites/... part) Library Shared Documents Folder Grant on <path to the statements folder> (covers both sub-folders); the job reads only 01 MONTHLY STATEMENTS, weekly skipped for now Entra app bank-stmt-dlh-reader, single tenant, no redirect URI Permission Microsoft Graph, Application, Files.SelectedOperations.Selected + read grant on the folder

Why a folder-level grant: the folder lives in the root site next to other operations documents. Sites.Selected would expose the whole site.

docs.title: 1. Create the app
docs.text:
1. https://entra.microsoft.com -> Entra ID -> App registrations -> New registration.
  2. Name bank-stmt-dlh-reader; account type Single tenant; no redirect URI; Register.
  3. On Overview copy Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID.

docs.title: 2. Create the client secret
docs.text:
1. Manage -> Certificates & secrets -> Client secrets -> New client secret (12 or 24 months).
  2. Copy the Value at once (not the Secret ID). It is shown only once.
  3. Calendar reminder 30 days before expiry; the job fails when it expires.

docs.title: 3. Add the permission
docs.text:
1. Manage -> API permissions -> Add a permission -> Microsoft Graph -> Application permissions.
  2. Add Files.SelectedOperations.Selected, then Grant admin consent. Status must show a green tick.

docs.title: 4. Fill .env (gitignored; never paste secrets in chat or git)
docs.text:
SP_TENANT_ID=<Directory (tenant) ID>
SP_CLIENT_ID=<Application (client) ID>
SP_CLIENT_SECRET=<secret Value>
SP_SITE_HOST=<tenant>.sharepoint.com
SP_SITE_PATH=
SP_LIBRARY=Shared Documents
SP_FOLDER=<path to the statements folder>
SP_SITE_ID=<from step 5.1, reference only>
SP_DRIVE_ID=<from step 5.2>
SP_FOLDER_ID=<from step 5.3, the year folder that holds the grant>
SP_MONTHLY_FOLDER_ID=<child '01 MONTHLY STATEMENTS' of the year folder; the job reads this one>
SP_WEEKLY_FOLDER_ID=<child '02 WEEKLY STATEMENTS'; not read for now>
The app can only read the granted folder, so it cannot look up sites or paths. The job uses SP_DRIVE_ID and SP_FOLDER_ID directly. They are not secret. No quotes, no spaces around =. Save the file.

docs.title: 5. Grant the app read on the folder (admin, one time)
docs.text:
The Entra permission alone gives no access: the app sees nothing until a folder is granted to it. Do this in Graph Explorer (https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), signed in as the tenant admin (check the profile icon; not a personal account).

5.0 Consent once (your own sign-in, not the app). Tab Modify permissions -> Consent for Sites.Read.All and Files.Read.All. Without it you get accessDenied: Request Doesn't have the required Permission scopes to access a site. Before the final POST also consent to Files.ReadWrite.All.

5.1 Site id. GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/<tenant>.sharepoint.com -> id (looks like <tenant>.sharepoint.com,<guid>,<guid>, with commas) -> SP_SITE_ID.

5.2 Drive id. GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/{site-id}/drives -> the entry named Documents -> id (starts with b!) -> SP_DRIVE_ID. Do not use /sites/{site-id}/root:/path; that is a Bad Request. Paths go through the drive.

5.3 Year folder id. GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/{drive-id}/root:/<path to the statements folder> -> id (starts with 01) -> SP_FOLDER_ID. A 404 means a folder name differs; list the parent with .../root:/<parent folder>:/children and compare names. Replace spaces with %20 if needed.

5.4 Grant. Method POST, URL https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/{drive-id}/items/{folder-id}/permissions, and the JSON in the Request body tab (under the URL bar; a blank tab gives Empty Payload. JSON content expected): 

{"roles":["read"],"grantedTo":{"application":{"id":"<SP_CLIENT_ID>","displayName":"bank-stmt-dlh-reader"}}}
Use grantedTo. The site-style grantedToIdentities is rejected on folders with 'grantedTo' must be provided. id is the app's Application (client) ID, not the object id or tenant id. Success is 201 Created with "roles":["read"] and the app name in the response. Allow a minute or two to take effect.

5.5 Sub-folder ids. The grant on the year folder covers its children. Read their ids: GET .../drives/{drive-id}/items/{folder-id}/children -> 01 MONTHLY STATEMENTS -> SP_MONTHLY_FOLDER_ID, 02 WEEKLY STATEMENTS -> SP_WEEKLY_FOLDER_ID (saved, not read for now). The job reads only the monthly folder.

Check a grant: GET .../drives/{drive-id}/items/{folder-id}/permissions lists bank-stmt-dlh-reader with role read. Revoke: DELETE .../items/{folder-id}/permissions/{permission-id} (the id from that list). Each new year: repeat 5.3-5.5 for the new OPSyyyy year folder and add its ids.
